name: Euro-area economy
value: Q3 GDP +0.4%; Nov flash composite PMI 51.7
summary: Euro-area flash composite PMI held at 51.7 in November; Q3 GDP grew 0.4%, so growth stays positive
state: The flash euro-area composite PMI was unchanged at 51.7 in November, slightly below expectations, with Germany driving growth while France's downturn deepened and the rest of the bloc grew at a six-month low (Trading Economics, 23 Nov). Eurostat put third-quarter GDP growth at 0.4% in the euro area. With growth positive and the PMI above 50, the signal stays Normal.
for_you: Euro-area activity is still expanding overall, though France is contracting. Households and firms exposed to France face a weaker local economy than the euro-area average suggests.
rubric_hit: Normal: Q3 GDP +0.4% (positive) and Nov flash composite PMI 51.7 > 50

sources.title: Trading Economics — Eurozone private sector growth holds steady in November
Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
